header: Onetime Secret - Full Environment Variable Reference
This file documents every supported environment variable.
* [derived] are generated by `rake ots:init` via HKDF from SECRET.
* [independent] are randomly generated by `rake ots:init` and must be backed up separately.
* [federation] must be set manually and shared identically across all regions.
A trailing `# Since vX.Y.Z` records the release a variable first shipped in;
`# Since unreleased` means it ships in the next one. A variable with no
marker predates v0.24.0. The marker is a comment about the variable, not
part of its value — drop it when copying a line, since `docker run
--env-file` and `docker compose --env-file` take the whole rest of the line
as the value rather than stripping a trailing comment.

records.name: SECRET
prose: Root secret. All derived secrets use HKDF (RFC 5869) with
this as input keying material. The only value needed for
disaster recovery. Treat it like the database itself: back it
up in a secret manager and never regenerate it casually — see
docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md for what depends on it and
how to rotate it safely.

records.name: SECRET_VERIFIER_MODE
prose: Boot-time SECRET verifier policy (site.secret_verifier_mode).
The app stores an HKDF-derived verifier in the datastore and checks
it on boot so a changed SECRET is detected instead of silently making
existing secrets undecryptable. warn (default) | enforce | off.

declaredDefault.evidence: existing secrets undecryptable. warn (default) | enforce | off.

records.name: SECRET_PREVIOUS
prose: Previous SECRET value(s), decrypt-only, for key rotation
(comma-separated, oldest first — append the outgoing SECRET on each
rotation). Old ciphertexts keep decrypting while new writes use the
current SECRET. Keep each entry for at least the longest secret TTL
plus receipt TTL, then drop it. See docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md.

records.name: SESSION_SECRET
prose: [derived] Rack session signing key

records.name: SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT
prose: Absolute session lifetime in seconds since sign-in, however active the
session is (site.session.absolute_timeout). site.session.expire_after is
the idle clock (24h rolling); this is the bound activity cannot slide.
Applies in both auth modes: to the session blob (from authenticated_at)
and, in full mode, to the active-session row (created_at), where it is
also Rodauth's session_lifetime_deadline. Remembered sessions end at
their own 14-day deadline first. Accepts a non-negative integer only;
anything else falls back to the default.
Default: 2592000 (30 days). Set to 0 to disable the bound (not
recommended).

records.name: IDENTIFIER_SECRET
prose: [derived] Secret link verification key (Familia::VerifiableIdentifier).
Used to generate secret/receipt keys. Derived from SECRET via HKDF.

records.name: AUTH_SECRET
prose: [independent] HMAC key for Rodauth auth operations (TOTP, login tokens).
Cannot be recovered from SECRET. Back this up.

records.name: ARGON2_SECRET
prose: [independent] Argon2 pepper for password hashing (full auth mode).
Folded into every password hash via Rodauth's argon2_secret.
Cannot be recovered from SECRET. WARNING: Changing this invalidates
ALL existing password hashes. Back this up.
See: apps/web/auth/config/features/argon2.rb

records.name: FEDERATION_SECRET
prose: [federation] Cross-region subscription federation.
Must be identical across all regions in a multi-region deploy.
Not auto-generated — set manually and share across instances.

records.name: ACCOUNT_ID_SECRET
prose: [independent] Obfuscates numeric account IDs in email-verification
links and remember-me cookies.
Also keys the pseudonymous Sentry diagnostics references
(Onetime::Utils::DiagnosticsRef): the actor reference is derived from the
customer's external identifier and the organization reference from the
organization objid, both HMAC'd under this secret and truncated. Sentry
receives only the opaque reference, never the identifier it was derived
from. Those references support issue correlation and affected-account
counts within this installation; they are not for product usage analytics
or behavioral profiling, and a keyed pseudonym is still potentially
personal data. Because both pre-images are minted per installation,
separately provisioned installations do not correlate — do not copy this
secret between installations. Rotating it re-keys every reference, so
correlation with already-reported events breaks; under Sentry's retention
window that discontinuity ages out on its own. With no secret set, no
references are emitted at all.

records.name: AUTH_OLD_SECRET
prose: Previous AUTH_SECRET value, set only while rotating AUTH_SECRET
(Rodauth hmac_old_secret). Tokens HMAC'd under the outgoing secret
keep validating during the rotation window; unset when done. Full
auth mode (AUTHENTICATION_MODE=full) only. No default.

records.name: RODAUTH_HMAC_SECRET
prose: [deprecated] Not consumed by this app — appears only in the vendored
Rodauth reference doc. The Rodauth HMAC secret is read from
AUTH_SECRET instead (hmac_secret_env_key 'AUTH_SECRET' in
apps/web/auth/config/base.rb). Set AUTH_SECRET; this var is ignored.

records.name: VERIFIABLE_ID_HMAC_SECRET
prose: HMAC key the familia gem reads to sign secret/receipt identifiers
(Familia::VerifiableIdentifier). When unset, boot fills it from
IDENTIFIER_SECRET, else HKDF-derives it from SECRET (purpose
:identifier). A set-but-blank value is kept and rejected by familia.
Set only to override; normally manage IDENTIFIER_SECRET instead.

records.name: VALKEY_REQUIRE_TLS
prose: Refuse to boot unless the datastore URI uses TLS (redis.require_tls):
rediss:// or valkeys://, with no `ssl` query parameter, whatever the host.
Either variable set to the exact string 'true' enables it. Off by default so
existing deployments keep booting; while off, a plaintext URI is reported
once at boot: a WARNING for a dotted hostname or public IP, an INFO line for
a single-label name (a compose service such as `maindb`) or a private, CGNAT
or link-local IP, nothing for loopback or a unix socket. Hostnames are never
resolved. Turn it on once the datastore serves TLS.

records.name: VALKEY_PASSWORD
prose: Password for the bundled Valkey/Redis datastore. REQUIRED by both
docker/compose/docker-compose.simple.yml and docker-compose.full.yml, which
set `valkey-server --requirepass` and refuse to start unless this is set. The
compose file threads the SAME value into the connection URL, so also embed
it in REDIS_URL/VALKEY_URL for non-compose deployments
(redis://:PASSWORD@host:6379/0). Use a URL-safe value (hex/alphanumeric — no
@ : / # so it needs no URL-encoding); generate one with:
echo "VALKEY_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" >> .env

records.name: RABBITMQ_USER
prose: RabbitMQ (job system). Broker credentials are REQUIRED by the bundled
docker/compose/docker-compose.full.yml — BOTH must be set or the stack
fails fast at `docker compose up`, before any container starts, with a
clear "RABBITMQ_USER must be set" / "RABBITMQ_PASS must be set" message.
This is deliberate and applies to the FULL STACK REGARDLESS of JOBS_ENABLED:
the broker, worker-email, and scheduler always run (they sit idle when
jobs are off — see docker/README.md "Background Jobs"), so their AMQP
identity must exist even in the default (jobs-off) configuration. The full
stack is a production deployment; this mirrors the SECRET fail-fast guard.
These two values seed the broker's default user AND are woven into the
app/worker/scheduler AMQP URLs by the compose file, so you do NOT set
RABBITMQ_URL yourself for the full stack (see the note below).
Never ship the historic guest/guest pair: RabbitMQ's 'guest' account is a
well-known default and (on newer RabbitMQ) is refused over non-loopback.

records.name: RABBITMQ_URL
prose: Full AMQP URL read directly by the app when it publishes jobs
(JOBS_ENABLED=true), via jobs.rabbitmq_url. Must carry the SAME credentials
as RABBITMQ_USER / RABBITMQ_PASS above. Format: amqp://USER:PASS@host:5672/vhost
NOTE: docker/compose/docker-compose.full.yml sets RABBITMQ_URL on the app,
worker-email, AND scheduler services itself — deriving it from RABBITMQ_USER /
RABBITMQ_PASS and pointing at the in-network broker (amqp://…@rabbitmq:5672,
default vhost '/'). That compose-set value overrides this one, so leave this
placeholder alone for the full stack. Set it only for non-compose or
external-broker deployments.

records.name: FAMILIA_POOL_SIZE
prose: Size of the shared Valkey/Redis connection pool used for all
Familia model operations (count of connections). Default: 25.

records.name: FAMILIA_POOL_TIMEOUT
prose: Seconds to wait when checking a connection out of the Valkey/Redis
connection pool before raising a timeout error. Default: 5.

records.name: REDIS_DBS_CUSTOM_DOMAIN
prose: Fallback alias for VALKEY_DBS_CUSTOM_DOMAIN
(redis.dbs.custom_domain); the VALKEY_ variant wins when both are
set. Logical database number 0-15. Default: 0.

records.name: REDIS_DBS_CUSTOMER
prose: Fallback alias for VALKEY_DBS_CUSTOMER (redis.dbs.customer); the
VALKEY_ variant wins when both are set. Logical database number
0-15. Default: 0.

records.name: REDIS_DBS_FEEDBACK
prose: Fallback alias for VALKEY_DBS_FEEDBACK (redis.dbs.feedback); the
VALKEY_ variant wins when both are set. Logical database number
0-15. Default: 0.

records.name: REDIS_DBS_METADATA
prose: Fallback alias for VALKEY_DBS_METADATA (redis.dbs.metadata); the
VALKEY_ variant wins when both are set. Logical database number
0-15. Default: 0.

records.name: REDIS_DBS_SECRET
prose: Fallback alias for VALKEY_DBS_SECRET (redis.dbs.secret); the
VALKEY_ variant wins when both are set. Logical database number
0-15. Default: 0.

records.name: VALKEY_DBS_CUSTOM_DOMAIN
prose: Logical database number for custom-domain records
(redis.dbs.custom_domain). 0-15, default 0. Takes precedence over
REDIS_DBS_CUSTOM_DOMAIN. Note: this mapping is currently
informational (shown in the boot banner); all models connect to the
database in the connection URL.

records.name: VALKEY_DBS_CUSTOMER
prose: Logical database number for customer records (redis.dbs.customer).
0-15, default 0. Takes precedence over REDIS_DBS_CUSTOMER. Note:
this mapping is currently informational (shown in the boot banner);
all models connect to the database in the connection URL.

records.name: VALKEY_DBS_FEEDBACK
prose: Logical database number for feedback records (redis.dbs.feedback).
0-15, default 0. Takes precedence over REDIS_DBS_FEEDBACK. Note:
this mapping is currently informational (shown in the boot banner);
all models connect to the database in the connection URL.

records.name: VALKEY_DBS_METADATA
prose: Logical database number for metadata (receipt) records
(redis.dbs.metadata). 0-15, default 0. Takes precedence over
REDIS_DBS_METADATA. Note: this mapping is currently informational
(shown in the boot banner); all models connect to the database in
the connection URL.

records.name: VALKEY_DBS_SECRET
prose: Logical database number for secret records (redis.dbs.secret).
0-15, default 0. Takes precedence over REDIS_DBS_SECRET. Note:
this mapping is currently informational (shown in the boot banner);
all models connect to the database in the connection URL.

records.name: HOST
prose: Public hostname. Include port if non-standard.

records.name: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE
prose: Explicit override for the session cookie's Secure flag; wins over any
SSL-derived value. In production SSL=false alone no longer disables Secure
(the app fails closed); set this to false ONLY for a deliberately plain-HTTP
deployment (the e2e lanes use it). Unset: derived from SSL / environment.

records.name: RACK_ENV
prose: Runtime environment

records.name: TTL_OPTIONS
prose: Available TTL choices for users (space-separated seconds).
5m   1h    1d    7d     30d

records.name: DEFAULT_TTL
prose: Default TTL when not specified (seconds). Default: 604800 (7 days)

records.name: TTL_MAX_ANONYMOUS
prose: Maximum TTL for secrets created without an account (seconds).
Default: 604800 (7 days). Max: 31536000 (365 days).
Clamped between 1 second and 365 days; invalid or non-positive values use the
default. The effective ceiling is the lower of this and the TTL_OPTIONS
maximum. Self-hosted deployments may raise it above 7 days; on deployments
with billing enabled the free-tier plan limit applies as an additional
ceiling, so anonymous callers never outrank an authenticated free-tier user.
On a billing-enabled deployment this variable also sets the free-tier
secret_lifetime fallback used when plan state is unavailable (default 1209600,
14 days, matching free_v1 in etc/billing.yaml), so it moves both values.
Replaces PLAN_TTL_ANONYMOUS, which is still read as a deprecated alias for the
anonymous ceiling when TTL_MAX_ANONYMOUS is unset, but no longer moves the
free-tier fallback. Rename it.
@see https://github.com/onetimesecret/onetimesecret/issues/2390

records.name: SECRET_CREATE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
prose: Rate limit on ANONYMOUS secret creation (site.secret_options.
create_rate_limit), counted per masked client IP (/24 IPv4, /48 IPv6)
across every creation entry point (V1/V2/V3 conceal and generate).
Authenticated callers are never charged. Enabled by default; set
ENABLED=false to opt out. The cap is deliberately loose — the bucket
is a whole /24 (office or campus NAT), and behind an unconfigured
reverse proxy it is the entire deployment — so raise MAX_PER_IP for
dense-NAT populations rather than tightening it.
See lib/onetime/security/conceal_secret_rate_limiter.rb.

records.name: SECRET_CREATE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP
prose: Anonymous creations permitted per window from one masked IP. Default: 500.

records.name: SECRET_CREATE_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW
prose: Counting window in seconds. Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: SECRET_CREATE_RATE_LIMIT_LOCKOUT
prose: Lockout duration in seconds once the cap is hit. Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: PASSPHRASE_ENFORCE_COMPLEXITY
prose: Require complexity in secret passphrases
(site.secret_options.passphrase.enforce_complexity). When true, the
V2 API rejects passphrases missing an uppercase letter, lowercase
letter, number, or symbol. Ignored by the V1 API (preserves v0.23.4
behavior). Default: false; set to 'true' to enable.

records.name: PASSPHRASE_MAX_LENGTH
prose: Maximum passphrase length in characters
(site.secret_options.passphrase.maximum_length). Secret creation
rejects longer passphrases on both V1 and V2 APIs. Default: 128.

records.name: PASSPHRASE_MIN_LENGTH
prose: Minimum passphrase length in characters
(site.secret_options.passphrase.minimum_length). Enforced on both
V1 and V2 APIs when a passphrase is provided. Default: 4.

records.name: PASSPHRASE_REQUIRED
prose: Require a passphrase on every secret
(site.secret_options.passphrase.required). When true, creating a
secret without a passphrase fails on both V1 and V2 APIs.
Default: false; set to 'true' to enable.

declaredDefault.evidence: Default: false; set to 'true' to enable.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_EXCLUDE_AMBIGUOUS
prose: Exclude visually ambiguous characters (0, O, o, 1, l, I, i) from
generated passwords (site.secret_options.password_generation
.character_sets.exclude_ambiguous). Generate requests may override
character_sets per call. Default: true; set to 'false' to allow
ambiguous characters.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_LENGTH
prose: Default length in characters for generated passwords
(site.secret_options.password_generation.default_length). Used when
a generate request does not specify its own length. Default: 12.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_LOWERCASE
prose: Include lowercase letters (a-z) in generated passwords
(site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.lowercase).
When multiple sets are enabled, at least one character from each is
guaranteed. Default: true; set to 'false' to exclude.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_MAX_LENGTH
prose: Server-enforced ceiling on the requested length of a generated password
(site.secret_options.password_generation.maximum_length). Oversized
`length` values are rejected before allocation, closing a memory-exhaustion
DoS on the anonymous generate endpoints. Matches the frontend Zod max so the
client and server limits stay in lockstep. Default: 128.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_NUMBERS
prose: Include numbers (0-9) in generated passwords
(site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.numbers).
When multiple sets are enabled, at least one character from each is
guaranteed. Default: true; set to 'false' to exclude.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_SYMBOLS
prose: Include symbols (!@#$%^&* etc.) in generated passwords
(site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.symbols).
When multiple sets are enabled, at least one character from each is
guaranteed. Default: true; set to 'false' to exclude.

records.name: PASSWORD_GEN_UPPERCASE
prose: Include uppercase letters (A-Z) in generated passwords
(site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.uppercase).
When multiple sets are enabled, at least one character from each is
guaranteed. Default: true; set to 'false' to exclude.

records.name: SECRET_MAX_LENGTH
prose: Maximum secret content size in characters
(site.secret_options.content.maximum_length). Server-enforced
ceiling on the secret body for V2 and incoming secrets; also the
single source of truth for the client-side textarea limit. The V1
API uses a fixed 10000-char limit instead. Default: 10000.

records.name: GENERATED_VALUE_DISPLAY_TTL
prose: Window in seconds after creation during which a generated
password's value may be revealed on the creator's receipt page
(site.secret_options.generated_value_display_ttl). Applies only to
generated secrets; the reveal is claimed atomically so it happens
at most once. Set to 0 to disable receipt-page display.
Default: 60.

records.name: SMTP_SSL
prose: Implicit TLS (SMTPS): the connection is encrypted from the start,
typically on port 465. When enabled it takes precedence over SMTP_TLS
and STARTTLS is not attempted. Default: false; set to 'true' to enable.

records.name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
prose: AWS access key for SES. Fallback credential for SES transactional
delivery when emailer.user (SMTP_USERNAME) is unset, and for SES
sender-domain provisioning when CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID is
unset. No default.

records.name: AWS_REGION
prose: AWS region for SES API clients: transactional delivery and the
suppression-list feedback sync. Fallback when the config region is
unset — emailer.region (EMAILER_REGION) for delivery,
email_providers.ses.region (CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_REGION) for the
feedback client. Default: us-east-1.

records.name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
prose: AWS secret key paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID. Fallback for SES
transactional delivery when emailer.pass (SMTP_PASSWORD) is unset,
and for SES sender-domain provisioning when
CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY is unset. No default.

records.name: EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE
prose: [deprecated] No effect. Formerly read by the legacy auth mailer
(removed); auth emails are delivered by the unified Onetime::Mail
system. To log emails instead of sending, use EMAILER_MODE=logger.

records.name: EMAIL_SUBJECT_PREFIX
prose: [deprecated] No effect. Formerly read by the legacy auth mailer
(removed). The live auth config hardcodes Rodauth's
email_subject_prefix to '' because templates carry their own
subject prefixes. No replacement.

records.name: FROM
prose: [deprecated] Use FROM_EMAIL instead. Legacy fallback for the sender
address (emailer.from); read only when FROM_EMAIL is unset. When
both are unset the placeholder CHANGEME@example.com is used.

records.name: REPLYTO_EMAIL
prose: Reply-To address for outbound email (emailer.reply_to). Falls back
to FROM_EMAIL when unset. Note: the current delivery path resolves
reply-to from template data or a domain's custom sender config, so
this config value has no runtime reader today.

records.name: SENDGRID_API_KEY
prose: SendGrid API key for transactional email delivery, used when the
provider resolves to sendgrid (EMAILER_MODE=sendgrid, or
auto-detected from an emailer.sendgrid_api_key config value).
Resolution order: emailer.sendgrid_api_key, then emailer.pass
(SMTP_PASSWORD), then this variable. No default.

records.name: SMTP_DOMAIN
prose: HELO domain for SMTP delivery (emailer.domain). Passed to the Mail
gem's :domain setting when non-empty; identifies this server to the
receiving SMTP server. Optional; unset by default (the mail library
then uses its own HELO default).

records.name: AUTHENTICATION_MODE
prose: 'full' enables Rodauth-based auth with PostgreSQL.
Other modes may use simpler auth flows.

records.name: AUTH_AUTOVERIFY
prose: false (default): new accounts must verify their email address before
signing in — requires a working SMTP/email provider config.
true: accounts are usable immediately after signup; the right choice for
private/team instances or installs without an email provider.

declaredDefault.evidence: false (default): new accounts must verify their email address before

records.name: AUTH_REQUIRED
prose: When true, the homepage secret form requires a signed-in user (site
navigation and branding remain visible). Default: false.

records.name: AUTH_EMAIL_AUTH_ENABLED
prose: Full-mode features

records.name: AUTH_PASSWORD_ONLY
prose: Restrict sign-in to a single authentication method. This is an access
control, not a display preference: every other method's routes 404 on
the restricted host, not just hide.
Set at most ONE of these to 'true'. The result maps to
full.restrict_to in auth config (values: password, email_auth,
webauthn, sso). Setting more than one is a FATAL BOOT ERROR naming
every flag set — there is no "restricted to two methods".
The named method must actually be available (feature enabled and
credentials present); if it is not, that is also a FATAL BOOT ERROR.
Post-boot or per-host unavailability degrades to "sign-in
unavailable" — never back to showing all methods.
If none are set, all enabled methods are shown (default).

records.name: ALLOWED_SIGNUP_DOMAIN
prose: Restrict account creation to specific email domains, comma-separated
(site.authentication.allowed_signup_domains), e.g. "company.com,
partner.org". Applies to password AND SSO signups; a custom domain's
own SignupConfig takes precedence when present. Empty/unset
(default): signups allowed from any domain.

records.name: RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
prose: Rate limiting for reset-password requests (#3872;
site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit). Throttles POST
/auth/reset-password-request per client IP and per submitted login
BEFORE any account lookup, bounding the sampling throughput of the
accepted timing residual from #3857. Applies in BOTH auth modes: full
mode enforces it from the Rodauth before_reset_password_request_route
hook, simple mode (the default) from the shared reset-request logic.
Enabled by
default (protective); set to the exact string 'false' to opt out —
other falsey-looking values ('0', 'no', 'off') leave it ENABLED, the
same convention as the other *_ENABLED != 'false' knobs in
etc/defaults/config.defaults.yaml.
See lib/onetime/security/reset_request_rate_limiter.rb.

records.name: RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP
prose: Requests permitted per window from a single client IP before the
per-IP tier locks out
(site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.max_per_ip). Default: 10.

records.name: RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_EMAIL
prose: Higher backstop cap per submitted login, catching IP-rotating callers
(site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.max_per_email).
Default: 30.

records.name: RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW
prose: Counting window in seconds for both rate-limit tiers
(site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.window).
Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_LOCKOUT
prose: Lockout duration in seconds once a tier's cap is hit
(site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.lockout).
Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
prose: Rate limiting for magic-link requests
(site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit). Throttles POST
/auth/email-login-request per client IP and per submitted login BEFORE any
account lookup, so one source cannot mail sign-in links to address after
address or sample the route for account existence. Full mode with
AUTH_EMAIL_AUTH_ENABLED=true only; the route does not exist otherwise.
Same two tiers as the reset-request limiter above, under separate keys.
Enabled by default (protective); set to the exact string 'false' to opt
out — other falsey-looking values leave it ENABLED.
See lib/onetime/security/reset_request_rate_limiter.rb.

records.name: EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP
prose: Requests permitted per window from a single client IP before the per-IP
tier locks out (site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.max_per_ip).
Default: 30 — looser than the reset-request cap because a magic link is a
sign-in method and a whole masked /24 shares the bucket. The same
TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED caveat as RESET_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP applies.
To clear a stuck lockout:
bin/ots ratelimit keys email_login_request_ip <masked-ip> | grep -v '^#' | valkey-cli
or POST /api/colonel/ratelimit/reset with kind=email_login_request_ip.

or POST /api/colonel/ratelimit/reset with kind=email_login_request_ip.

records.name: EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_EMAIL
prose: Backstop cap per submitted login, catching IP-rotating callers
(site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.max_per_email).
Default: 90. Keep it at least 2 x EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP,
and EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_LOCKOUT at least
EMAIL_LOGIN_REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW: a single IP timing its requests
around its own window boundary lands up to 2 x max_per_ip - 2 requests in
one login's window, and with a shorter lockout it is free again inside that
window, so one source could lock a victim out of magic-link sign-in from
every IP. The defaults satisfy both. Rodauth's resend window already caps
the mail an account receives.

records.name: CREATE_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
prose: Rate limiting for unauthenticated account creation
(site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit). POST /auth/create-account
previously had no limiter in EITHER auth mode, leaving unthrottled account
creation: one customer record (which carries no TTL) plus one welcome email
per distinct address, with subaddressing folding many addresses onto one
mailbox. This setting applies to both modes — full mode enforces it from the
Rodauth before_create_account_route hook, simple mode from the shared
CreateAccount logic class — so the knob means the same thing whichever mode
a deployment runs.
Enabled by default (protective); set to the exact string 'false' to opt out
— other falsey-looking values ('0', 'no', 'off') leave it ENABLED, the same
convention as the other *_ENABLED != 'false' knobs.
See lib/onetime/security/create_account_rate_limiter.rb.

records.name: CREATE_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_PER_IP
prose: Signups permitted per window from a single client IP before the limiter
locks out (site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.max_per_ip).
Default: 10.

records.name: CREATE_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW
prose: Counting window in seconds
(site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.window).
Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: CREATE_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_LOCKOUT
prose: Lockout duration in seconds once the cap is hit
(site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.lockout).
Default: 3600 (1 hour).

records.name: AUTH_REMEMBER_ME_ENABLED
prose: Remember-me: the sign-in form's "Remember me" checkbox (auth:
full.features.remember_me) makes THAT session last a fixed 14 days from
sign-in instead of the rolling 24 hours; activity does not extend it.
Both auth modes. Set to 'false' to ignore the checkbox; sessions already
remembered return to the default lifetime (their 14-day deadline still
ends them). SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT still caps every session.
Default: true.

records.name: AUTH_SERVICE_URL
prose: Reserved: auth service base URL for internal requests (auth:
full.service_url). Currently inert — the config line is commented
out in etc/defaults/auth.defaults.yaml (example default
http://127.0.0.1:3000/auth) and the external-auth token validator
that would consume a service_url is an unimplemented placeholder.

records.name: AUTH_WEBAUTHN_AUTOFILL
prose: Enables Rodauth's webauthn_autofill feature: passkey autofill
(browser conditional UI) on the login form (auth:
full.features.webauthn_autofill). Default: false. Only the literal
string 'true' enables — any other value (including '1', 'yes', or
mere presence) leaves it off. Requires AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ENABLED=true
and AUTHENTICATION_MODE=full.

records.name: AUTH_WEBAUTHN_VERIFY_ACCOUNT
prose: Enables Rodauth's webauthn_verify_account feature: account email
verification sets up a WebAuthn credential instead of a password
(passwordless signup) (auth: full.features.webauthn_verify_account).
Default: false. Only the literal string 'true' enables — any other
value (including '1', 'yes', or mere presence) leaves it off.
Requires AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ENABLED=true and AUTHENTICATION_MODE=full;
leave AUTH_VERIFY_ACCOUNT_ENABLED on.

records.name: ENABLE_ORGS
prose: Toggle on to show the Organizations context switcher in the UI, next to
the equivalent Domain context switcher. This allows users to update their
default organization settings and add additional organizations to their
account. When billing is enabled, the subscription plans are per-org.

records.name: ORGS_SSO_ENABLED
prose: When enabled, allows organizations with the manage_sso entitlement to
configure SSO for each of their custom domains.

records.name: ORGS_CUSTOM_MAIL_ENABLED
prose: When enabled, allows organizations with the custom_mail_sender entitlement
to configure custom sender identity (from name, from address) for their
domains. Uses installation-level email provider credentials.

records.name: ORGS_INCOMING_SECRETS_ENABLED
prose: When enabled, allows organizations with the incoming_secrets entitlement
to configure incoming secret receiving for their custom domains. Secrets
sent to the domain are routed to the organization's inbox.

records.name: ORGS_HOMEPAGE_NETWORK_RULES_UI_ENABLED
prose: When enabled, allows organizations with the homepage_network_rules
entitlement to limit their custom domain homepages by client network
(allowed/denied CIDRs). Despite the name, this gates the API as well as
the UI: while off, PUT /api/domains/:extid/homepage-config refuses any
request that changes allowed_cidrs or denied_cidrs, and DELETE refuses to
drop a config that holds them. A list sent back unchanged is accepted.
Turning it off stops edits only: stored rules stay enforced.

records.name: ORGS_BASE_DOMAIN_SIGNUP_ENABLED
prose: When enabled, allows organizations with the base_domain_signup entitlement
to admit their custom domain's own base domain to its sign-up allowlist
automatically (secrets.acme.com admits @acme.com). Checked at sign-up too,
so turning it off stops a saved setting from admitting anyone.

records.name: ORGS_AUDIT_LOGS_ENABLED
prose: When enabled (the default), organizations with the audit_logs entitlement
can view their secret activity trail (UI + list API). Unlike the flags
above, this defaults ON because the trail works out of the box — set to
false to exclude the feature. Event collection is not affected.

records.name: SECRET_ACTIVITY_COLLECT
prose: Whether organization secret-activity events are recorded at all (GDPR
data minimization). Enabled by default; set to false to pause collection.
Pausing stops new events from being recorded — existing events stay
readable (pair with ORGS_AUDIT_LOGS_ENABLED=false to also hide them).

records.name: SECRET_ACTIVITY_MAX_EVENTS
prose: Newest secret-activity events retained per organization (floor: 100).
LOWERING this value DELETES (not hides) the oldest events past the new
cap in each org's trail, applied lazily on that org's next recorded
event. Setting SECRET_ACTIVITY_COLLECT=false does not trigger the trim.

sections.heading: Custom Mail Sender DNS Settings
prose: These settings control DNS record generation for DKIM, SPF, and related
email authentication when setting up custom mail sender domains.
The provider is selected by CUSTOM_MAIL_PROVIDER (above); these settings
configure that provider's DNS record values.

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_PROVIDER
prose: Provider for custom mail sender domain provisioning (DNS/DKIM).
Decouples domain provisioning from the sending transport above.
Valid values: ses, sendgrid, lettermint, smtp2go, smtp
If unset, falls back to EMAILER_MODE.

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_REGION
prose: --- AWS SES ---
Select SES as the sender-domain provisioning provider with
CUSTOM_MAIL_PROVIDER=ses (above). See docs/architecture/custom-mail-sender-ses.md
for the full domain-level setup, credentials, and IAM permissions.
AWS region for SES sender-domain provisioning (the SESv2 API client used to
create/get/delete email identities). This is INDEPENDENT of EMAILER_REGION,
which configures the install-level transactional mailer — so you can run, e.g.,
SMTP for transactional email and SES for sender provisioning.
Data-residency regions: ca-central-1 (Canada), ap-southeast-2 (Sydney),
eu-west-1 (Ireland). Confirm SES is available in your target region.
Default: us-east-1

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID
prose: AWS credentials for the SES provisioning API, kept independent of the SMTP
transactional mailer. If you run authenticated SMTP for delivery
(EMAILER_MODE=smtp with SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD), set these (or the
standard AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, which they fall back to)
so the SMTP login is NOT used as the AWS key for SES. Leave unset only when
SES is also the delivery backend (EMAILER_MODE=ses) and the emailer already
carries the AWS keys.

records.name: LETTERMINT_API_TOKEN
prose: --- Lettermint ---
Lettermint has TWO separate APIs with different auth:
1. Sending API - uses x-lettermint-token header (project token)
2. Team API    - uses Authorization: Bearer header (team token)
Project token for Lettermint Sending API (email delivery).
Required when EMAILER_MODE=lettermint

records.name: LETTERMINT_TEAM_TOKEN
prose: Team token for Lettermint Team API (domain provisioning).
Required for custom mail sender domain management (ORGS_CUSTOM_MAIL_ENABLED=true)
https://dash.lettermint.co/team/api-tokens

records.name: LETTERMINT_BASE_URL
prose: API base URL (for enterprise/on-premise deployments).
Default: https://api.lettermint.co/v1

records.name: SMTP2GO_API_KEY
prose: --- SMTP2GO ---
SMTP2GO (Christchurch, NZ) backs the NZ region. A single API key
covers API-based sending and sender-domain verification, authenticated
via the X-Smtp2go-Api-Key header.
API key from Sending > API Keys in the SMTP2GO dashboard.
Format: `api-` followed by 32 characters.
Required when EMAILER_MODE=smtp2go or CUSTOM_MAIL_PROVIDER=smtp2go

records.name: SMTP2GO_BASE_URL
prose: API base URL override; rarely needed.
Default: https://api.smtp2go.com/v3

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_RETURNPATH_SUBDOMAIN
prose: Return-path subdomain prefix for SMTP2GO sender-domain DNS records
(email_providers.smtp2go.returnpath_subdomain). Becomes a CNAME record
on the customer's sender domain (bounce.yourdomain.com) so the envelope
sender aligns for SPF. Default: bounce

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_TRACKING_SUBDOMAIN
prose: Tracking subdomain prefix for SMTP2GO sender-domain DNS records
(email_providers.smtp2go.tracking_subdomain). Becomes a CNAME record
on the customer's sender domain (track.yourdomain.com) for open/click
tracking. Default: track

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_FASTACCEPT
prose: Accept SMTP2GO messages asynchronously for faster API responses.
When enabled, synchronous rejection details are unavailable; use webhooks
for delivery results. Leave disabled for sender-configuration test emails
and only enable if you aren't running the background workers and you
find that requests the trigger an email send are taking too long to load.
Default: false

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_LETTERMINT_SPF_CNAME_PREFIX
prose: SPF CNAME subdomain prefix for Lettermint sender-domain DNS records
(email_providers.lettermint.spf_cname_prefix). 'lm-bounces' creates
lm-bounces.yourdomain.com pointing at the SPF CNAME target below.
Default: lm-bounces

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_LETTERMINT_SPF_CNAME_TARGET
prose: SPF CNAME target domain for Lettermint sender-domain DNS records
(email_providers.lettermint.spf_cname_target). Lettermint maintains
the SPF record at this target. Default: bounces.lmta.net

records.name: CUSTOM_MAIL_SENDGRID_SUBDOMAIN
prose: Branding subdomain prefix for SendGrid sender-domain DNS records
(email_providers.sendgrid.subdomain); appears in the generated
CNAME record names. Letters, digits, and hyphens only. Default: em

records.name: AUTH_SSO_ENABLED
prose: Master toggle for SSO. Must be true for any provider below.

records.name: SSO_DISPLAY_NAME
prose: [deprecated] Use per-provider DISPLAY_NAME vars instead.

records.name: OIDC_ISSUER
prose: --- Generic OIDC provider ---
Required: OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID
Optional: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET (omit for PKCE-only flows)

records.name: OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME
prose: Sign-in button label for this provider. Default: SSO

records.name: OIDC_CLIENT_AUTH_METHOD
prose: How the client secret is sent to the token endpoint: client_secret_basic
(Authorization: Basic header; the default when unset) or client_secret_post
(request body). Leave unset unless the IdP requires one method. An unknown
value is logged at boot and treated as unset. Custom-domain OIDC has its own
per-domain setting and never inherits this value.

records.name: OIDC_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.

records.name: ENTRA_TENANT_ID
prose: --- Microsoft Entra ID ---
Required: ENTRA_TENANT_ID, ENTRA_CLIENT_ID, ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET

records.name: ENTRA_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.

records.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
prose: --- GitHub ---
Required: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET

records.name: GITHUB_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.

records.name: GITLAB_CLIENT_ID
prose: --- GitLab ---
Required: GITLAB_CLIENT_ID, GITLAB_CLIENT_SECRET
gitlab.com only. For a self-managed GitLab, use the generic OIDC
provider above with OIDC_ISSUER set to the instance URL.

records.name: GITLAB_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.

records.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
prose: --- Google ---
Required: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET

records.name: GOOGLE_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.

records.name: APPLE_CLIENT_ID
prose: --- Apple (Sign in with Apple) ---
Required: APPLE_CLIENT_ID, APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_KEY_ID, APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY
APPLE_CLIENT_ID is the Services ID (e.g. com.example.web), not the App ID.
There is deliberately NO APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET: the strategy mints a fresh
ES256 client-secret JWT per request from the private key below.

records.name: APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY
prose: The CONTENTS of the .p8 EC key, not a path to it: the whole file, PEM
header and footer lines included. OpenSSL must be able to parse it, so the
newlines have to survive your env plumbing. The single-line form with each
newline written as a literal \n is accepted — the provider definition
un-escapes it before handing it to the strategy. (No sample value is shown
here: a realistic one trips the detect-private-key pre-commit hook.)

records.name: APPLE_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.
Apple's email may be a private relay address (@privaterelay.appleid.com),
which is not evidence of control over the underlying mailbox. Keep this
false. (The email itself arrives on every authorization, from the id_token;
only the user's NAME is limited to the first authorization.)

records.name: SAML_ENABLED
prose: Install-wide switch that turns SAML on. Default false. Unless true, the app
processes no SAML at all, on both surfaces: no saml route is registered
(platform SAML_* settings and every tenant's saved SAML config included, so
omniauth-saml/ruby-saml are not loaded), the SAML callback answers 404, the
sign-in button is not shown, and the per-domain SSO API refuses to save or
edit a SAML configuration (tenants can still disable or delete theirs).
Saved configurations are kept, untouched, and resume when it is set back
to true. This is an incident switch for a ruby-saml advisory: it stops
SAML without taking OIDC and Entra tenants down (ORGS_SSO_ENABLED=false
does). WARNING: custom domains restricted to SSO sign-in and using SAML
have NO sign-in method while this is off. Accepts the shared boolean
vocabulary (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off); any other value fails boot.
UPGRADING: an install that already has SAML_* set for platform SAML, or
tenants with saved SAML configs, must set this to true before upgrading or
SAML sign-in stops. See docs/authentication/per-install-sso.md.

records.name: SAML_IDP_SSO_SERVICE_URL
prose: Required (with SAML_ENABLED=true): SAML_IDP_SSO_SERVICE_URL,
SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID, SAML_IDP_CERT
There is no client id/secret: trust is the IdP's pinned signing certificate.
A missing OR unusable value skips the provider with an error in the boot log
(it never fails boot) and the login button is not shown.
The IdP's SSO endpoint (HTTP-Redirect binding). https only. The CSP
form-action origin and the cross-site POST callback allowance are derived
from THIS url's origin, not from the EntityID.

records.name: SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID
prose: The IdP's EntityID, exactly as the IdP sends it in <Issuer> — compared byte
for byte (case, trailing slash and all), and stored as the issuer half of
every SAML identity. Changing it later orphans existing SAML sign-ins.

records.name: SAML_IDP_CERT
prose: The CONTENTS of the IdP's X.509 signing certificate in PEM form, header and
footer lines included — exactly one certificate, not expired. The
single-line form with each newline written as a literal \n is accepted.
Certificate FINGERPRINTS are not supported, deliberately: fingerprint-only
trust accepts whatever certificate the response embeds. When the IdP rotates
its certificate this value must be updated (one certificate at a time).

records.name: SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID
prose: Our SP EntityID (the Audience the IdP must send). Default:
https://<site.host>/auth/sso/<route name>/metadata — which is also where the
SP metadata XML is served. The Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL to
register at the IdP is https://<site.host>/auth/sso/<route name>/callback
(HTTP-POST binding).

records.name: SAML_UID_ATTRIBUTE
prose: Use this SAML attribute as the stable user id instead of the NameID. Required
when the IdP can only send a TRANSIENT NameID (refused otherwise — a
transient id would create a new account on every sign-in). The IdP should
send a persistent NameID (requested by default).

records.name: SAML_NAME_ID_FORMAT
prose: NameID format requested from the IdP and accepted in the response. Default
persistent. Also accepted: the SAML 1.1 emailAddress and unspecified formats,
the 2.0 transient format (needs SAML_UID_ATTRIBUTE; the provider is skipped
at boot without it), or 'omit' to send no NameIDPolicy at all. Existing
identities are keyed on the NameID and will not match after a format change
unless SAML_UID_ATTRIBUTE supplies the key. Tenant records carry their own
name_id_format. See docs/authentication/saml-policy.md.

records.name: SAML_ALLOW_NULL_ORIGIN
prose: Operator-only: admit a literal 'Origin: null' header on POSTs to a configured
SAML callback route, for IdP flows that submit an opaque origin. Only the
exact string true enables it; unset, false and any other spelling deny. No
tenant setting can enable this. See docs/authentication/saml-policy.md.

records.name: SAML_CALLBACK_SOURCE_LIMIT
prose: Staging admission for the SAML callback transport, per fixed 120-second
bucket: how many staged assertions one privacy-masked client source may
take, and the global cap shared by every host (the deployment-wide storage
bound). Positive integers up to 1000000; the source limit is clamped to the
global limit; an invalid value logs a warning and uses the default. Raising
them increases storage exposure. See docs/authentication/saml-callback-transport.md.

records.name: SAML_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.
SAML carries no email_verified claim: the email attribute is whatever the IdP
asserts.

records.name: SSO_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS
prose: Extra origins for the CSP form-action directive (space-separated).
IdP origins are auto-derived on two levels: each active platform
provider's origin is added at boot, and a custom domain's tenant SSO
issuer origin is added per-request from its per-domain SSO config
(#4173) — so Chromium does not block the SSO form-POST redirect on
either surface. Configure sovereign Microsoft Entra as generic OIDC
with its sovereign issuer; that origin is derived automatically. Set
this only when the auto-derived origin is wrong or incomplete: an OIDC
issuer whose authorization_endpoint lives on a different origin than
the issuer, or a per-request tenant derivation gap. The tenant widening
depends on the resolved display domain: if the domain record is
unreachable at request time it is skipped silently (browser-console-only
symptom), and this override is the manual fallback for such gap cases.

records.name: SSO_PROVIDER_ORDER
prose: Login-button ordering for SSO providers: a comma/space-separated list of
route names (e.g. "google, github, oidc"). Listed providers appear first
in the given order; unlisted ones keep their registry order after them.
Unset = registry order (lib/onetime/sso_provider/registry.rb).

records.name: SSO_ALLOW_PLATFORM_FALLBACK
prose: Multi-tenant SSO fallback policy (auth:
full.sso.allow_platform_fallback_for_tenants). When true, custom
domains without their own per-domain SSO config may piggyback on the
platform's ENV-based SSO credentials — convenient for single-tenant,
a security concern in multi-tenant. Default: false ('true' enables).

records.name: SSO_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
prose: Global/deprecated fallback for the per-provider *_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING vars
above (single-OIDC case; a per-provider var, when set, takes precedence).
Default false. Opt-in email-based SSO linking; single-tenant trusted-IdP only.
Opting a single provider OUT of a global true requires an EXPLICIT =false:
with SSO_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING=true, a provider whose *_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
is simply omitted INHERITS the global true. To disable one provider, set it
explicitly, e.g. GITHUB_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING=false.

records.name: GITHUB_KEY
prose: [deprecated] Not consumed by this app — appears only in the vendored
Rodauth reference doc. Use GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: the GitHub SSO
provider's OAuth client id (with GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET).

records.name: GITHUB_SECRET
prose: [deprecated] Not consumed by this app — appears only in the vendored
Rodauth reference doc. Use GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: the GitHub SSO
provider's OAuth client secret (with GITHUB_CLIENT_ID).

records.name: GOOGLE_KEY
prose: [deprecated] Not consumed by this app — appears only in the vendored
Rodauth reference doc. Use GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: the Google SSO
provider's OAuth client id (with GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET).

records.name: GOOGLE_SECRET
prose: [deprecated] Not consumed by this app — appears only in the vendored
Rodauth reference doc. Use GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: the Google SSO
provider's OAuth client secret (with GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID).

records.name: STRIPE_CHECKOUT_HOST
prose: Bare host of a Stripe custom Checkout domain (live-mode only), e.g.
pay.onetimesecret.com. When set, the frontend allowlists checkout URLs
served from this host in addition to checkout.stripe.com. Leave unset
unless a Stripe custom domain is configured. Wins over billing.yaml
`checkout_host`. Validated at boot when billing is enabled — the check runs
in Billing::Initializers::StripeSetup (BillingConfig#validate_checkout_host!),
which is skipped when billing is disabled. A malformed value
(scheme/path/userinfo/out-of-range port) fails startup, not a later checkout.

records.name: STRIPE_AUTOMATIC_TAX
prose: Enable Stripe automatic tax on checkout sessions. 'true'/'1' enable,
'false'/'0' disable, unset or blank means off; any other value fails
startup (Onetime::ConfigError) — an unrecognized token used to silently
disable tax collection. Deployment-level policy applied by
BillingConfig#automatic_tax? to all checkout sessions — not a per-link
choice. Wins over billing.yaml `automatic_tax`. Requires Stripe Tax to be
configured in the Dashboard (tax registrations + product tax codes) first.

records.name: STRIPE_PAYMENT_METHOD_CONFIGURATION
prose: Stripe payment method configuration ID (pmc_...) to pin on checkout
sessions. When set, checkout uses this specific configuration instead
of the Dashboard default. Wins over billing.yaml
`payment_method_configuration`. Leave unset to use the Dashboard
default. A blank-but-set value is treated as explicitly unset and does
NOT fall back to the billing.yaml key. A malformed value (anything not
starting with pmc_) fails startup (Onetime::ConfigError) when billing

sections.heading: Reverse Proxy / Client IP
prose: Site-wide client IP resolution (config site.network.trusted_proxy).
Affects ban checks, session tracking, audit logs, rate limiting, and the
Colonel "Your Current IP" display.
WARNING: Only enable when the app is behind a trusted reverse proxy, direct
client access is blocked by firewall, and the proxy strips/overwrites
client-provided forwarding headers.

records.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED
prose: Turns proxy-aware IP resolution on. The mode, CIDR, and depth settings
below do nothing while this is false.
When false (default), forwarded headers are ignored and the client IP is
REMOTE_ADDR (the address that opened the connection). That is right only
when clients connect to the app directly: put a proxy in front and
REMOTE_ADDR is the proxy, so every request looks like it came from one
address. When true, the client IP is read out of the forwarded headers
using the mode below. Behind a proxy you trust, set this to true. Behind one
you don't trust to overwrite X-Forwarded-For, set true and set the mode
below to depth, which picks the client by its position in the chain.

declaredDefault.evidence: When false (default), forwarded headers are ignored and the client IP is

records.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_MODE
prose: How to resolve client IP behind proxies. Default: filter.
- filter: CIDR-walk. Walk the forwarded chain LEFT-TO-RIGHT and return the
first entry that is not a trusted proxy — i.e. the LEFTMOST non-proxy
entry becomes the client IP. Trusted = RFC1918/loopback/link-local
fe80::/10) plus every range in TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS. Works for most
k8s/cloud deployments where proxies have internal IPs.
SECURITY: because the leftmost entry wins, the edge proxy MUST OVERWRITE
X-Forwarded-For with the real peer address, otherwise a client-supplied
entry is returned as the client IP and IP rate limits/bans are spoofable:
nginx:  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
Caddy:  header_up X-Forwarded-For {client_ip}
({client_ip} honours Caddy's own trusted_proxies, so it resolves the real
visitor when Caddy is itself behind a declared CDN; with none declared it
is the direct peer, same as {remote_host}. See etc/examples/Caddyfile-example.)
Use depth mode when you cannot make the edge overwrite. Combining the
overwrite above with depth mode is correct ONLY for TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH=1
(the overwrite leaves exactly one attested entry, which depth 1 selects);
a depth of 2 or more needs each counted hop to append one entry, and the
overwrite collapses that chain, so resolution falls back to the peer.
Note: filter mode reads the X-Forwarded-For family only (X-Forwarded-For,
X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP) and REJECTS any other TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER at boot.
- depth:  position-based; skip exactly TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH rightmost hops.
Counts positions from the RIGHT of the chain, so extra leftmost entries
(forged or from farther upstream) never shift the selection. Requires a
FIXED hop count with each counted hop appending exactly one entry: a
chain shorter than the depth falls back to the peer, and a depth larger
than the real hop count selects a client-supplied entry. Use for proxies
with public IPs that filter mode would misread as the client, or when
you need deterministic hop selection regardless of IP class.
Matched case-insensitively and canonicalized (as TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER is).
Anything outside the closed set falls back to filter — the safer mode — and
WARNs at boot naming the value; the startup `trusted_proxy:` posture line
always reports the mode actually in force, not the value configured here.

records.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER
prose: depth mode only: which header to read the forwarding chain from.
Default: X-Forwarded-For. The accepted set is closed — exactly one of:
- X-Forwarded-For  the de facto standard, written by nginx, Caddy, HAProxy,
ALB/ELB, Cloudflare, Fastly, and most k8s ingresses
- Forwarded        RFC 7239 (for=/by=/proto=), emitted by HAProxy and Apache
when configured for it; still uncommon in practice
- Both             read Forwarded first, fall back to X-Forwarded-For
Case-insensitive, so `forwarded` is accepted and canonicalized. Any other
value fails the boot with an ArgumentError rather than silently resolving
from the wrong header.
Vendor client-IP headers are NOT selectable here — CF-Connecting-IP,
True-Client-IP and friends are never read for client-IP resolution. They
also carry a single address rather than a chain, so there are no hops to
count. (Vendor GEO headers such as CF-IPCountry are a separate concern with
its own resolution path; this setting does not affect them.) If your
edge only sets one of those, have it write the chain into X-Forwarded-For:
Cloudflare: enable "Add visitor IP headers" (sets X-Forwarded-For), or
transform-rule X-Forwarded-For = cf.connecting_ip
Filter mode reads the X-Forwarded-For family only (X-Forwarded-For,
X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP) and never RFC 7239 Forwarded: with
TRUSTED_PROXY_MODE=filter, any value here other than X-Forwarded-For FAILS
THE BOOT with a message naming both settings. Leave it at the default (or
unset) unless the mode is depth.

records.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS
prose: filter mode only: additional CIDR ranges to trust as proxies beyond the
RFC1918 defaults (e.g. a CDN/proxy with public IPs). Comma-separated.
SECURITY: listing a range here is a full infrastructure-trust grant, not
just client-IP trust. Requests arriving from these ranges also have their
X-Forwarded-Host honored for custom-domain detection. It is the only
forwarded host header the application reads, and only when it holds one
value. The proxy MUST therefore overwrite it itself rather than pass it
through or append to it — a pass-through proxy lets a client pick the
tenant domain the app renders, and a comma-separated value is not read
at all (the request resolves on Host, with a WARN). This is the same
requirement stated above for X-Forwarded-For, extended to the host
header. Apx-Incoming-Host, X-Original-Host and RFC 7239 Forwarded's
host= parameter are never a host source: an edge that carries the public
host only there must preserve Host or send X-Forwarded-Host instead,
and should remove them. See docs/operations/proxy-authority-header.md.

records.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH
prose: depth mode only: number of proxy hops to skip from the right. Default: 1.
1 = standard single reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy)
2 = CDN -> reverse proxy -> app
For direct/no-proxy deployments set TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED=false above
rather than depth: 0.

records.name: GEO_DB_PATH
prose: Optional path to a local MaxMind country database (.mmdb) for deployments

records.name: SECRET_ACTIVITY_GEO_COUNTRY_ENABLED
prose: Country column on the org Secret Activity trail (config
